audit_notes: Critical parameter check: the proposed daytime-mean evaporative flux of 30 W/m2 assumes 0.12 kg/kg uptake. In hot-dry climates night RH is typically 20-40 percent, where silica gel takes ~0.05-0.10 kg/kg and sepiolite/attapulgite clays ~0.03-0.06 kg/kg; uptake is further limited by vapour diffusion through a porous ceramic skin within one night (diffusion time for 3-5 mm of sorbent ~hours). A realistic sustained value is ~0.18 kg/m2 per night -> 0.43 MJ/m2 over 8 h = 15 W/m2. I set effective_evaporative_flux to 15 W/m2 and water_uptake_fraction to 0.06. Also, in hot-humid climates uptake is high but daytime desorption at 40-50 C surface temperature is weak; either way the effect is modest. Dust and salt deposits reduce capacity over years. Dimensionless: Lewis number of air ~0.85; Biot envelope 0.026. Simulation coefficient: equivalent sol-air reduction effective_evaporative_flux/h_o = 0.75 K. Model: steady 1D conduction, analytical, with the evaporative sink at the outer surface. Baseline: aged cool paint (alpha 0.32, eps 0.90) without sorption. Expected gain ~6 percent. Mechanical: repeated wet/dry cycling of clays causes shrink-swell cracking of the skin; frost is not an issue in hot climates. Audit passed.
